title: Maximum Performance of a Team
summary: Given two integers n and k , along with two integer arrays speed and efficiency each of length n , where speed[i] and efficiency[i] represent the speed and efficiency of the i -th engineer respectively, select at most k engineers to form a team.
statement: Given two integers n and k , along with two integer arrays speed and efficiency each of length n , where speed[i] and efficiency[i] represent the speed and efficiency of the i -th engineer respectively, select at most k engineers to form a team. The performance of the team is defined as the sum of the speeds of the selected engineers multiplied by the minimum efficiency among the selected engineers. Determine the maximum possible performance of such a team, and return the result modulo 10^9 + 7 .
constraints: speed and efficiency describe n engineers; choose one through k of them.
Team performance is total speed multiplied by its minimum efficiency.
Maximize the unmodded performance, then return it modulo 1000000007.
hints: Process engineers from greatest efficiency to least.
At each engineer, current efficiency is the minimum for any team formed from the processed prefix.
Keep the k largest processed speeds in a min-heap and test current speed sum times current efficiency.
Every optimal team is considered when its least-efficient member is processed.
editorial: Sort by decreasing efficiency. A min-heap retains the largest k speeds among engineers whose efficiencies are at least the current threshold. Their sum times the current efficiency is the best team using that threshold; maximize before modulo. The oracle independently enumerates all allowed engineer subsets on seeded inputs.

tests.explanation: Engineers with speeds ten and five have total speed fifteen and minimum efficiency four, giving sixty.
The engineer with speed eight alone gives performance fifty-six.
